RISKSHOCKCONTINUATION_SHORT_KILLED_GATE_.thesis: Genuinely new cross-asset thesis (first ever attempted on USDMXN, not ported from US500/NASDAQ). USDMXN's price discovery lags US500's by several minutes during risk shocks; this edge fades extreme-upper-tail US500 5-minute up-shocks, betting USDMXN continues falling (lagged catch-up).
RISKSHOCKCONTINUATION_SHORT_KILLED_GATE_.diagnosis: Statistically validated BEFORE building: conditioning on top-2%-tail US500 5-min up-moves (n=2408), USDMXN's forward 2-bar return averaged -0.000249 vs an unconditional baseline of -0.0000027 (t-stat=-10.4). Not drift, not noise.
RISKSHOCKCONTINUATION_SHORT_KILLED_GATE_.gate_a_result: FAILED at 0/112 geometries (36 default hour-scale + 76 fine minute-scale, vertical_horizon swept 5min-2h). Best net_mean_R=-0.0544 (hour-scale default grid). Critically, gross_mean_R was SOMETIMES POSITIVE at the fine grid (up to +0.009 at vertical_horizon=2h) -- this is NOT a dead/non-existent signal like the other 16 mechanisms, whose gross was flat-to-negative everywhere. Here cost_mean_R (0.08-0.11) dwarfed the positive gross at every geometry tested.
RISKSHOCKCONTINUATION_SHORT_KILLED_GATE_.root_cause: The triple-barrier's 1R sizing (sl*Event_Vol) uses an EWM-smoothed historical volatility estimate that underestimates the AMBIENT volatility specifically during the shock episodes this edge selects for (extreme US500 tail moves plausibly co-occur with elevated near-term USDMXN volatility that the smoothed estimate lags). This inflates cost_mean_R disproportionately for this event population relative to an unconditional one.
RISKSHOCKCONTINUATION_SHORT_KILLED_GATE_.disposition: KILLED at Gate A, but flagged as 'real signal, not survivable under current R-normalization' rather than 'no real edge' -- the distinction the research prompt asks to track. A possible refinement (not pursued further this cycle): size R off shock-conditional realized vol rather than the generic smoothed EWM estimate. Folder kept on disk.
RISKSHOCKCONTINUATION_SHORT_KILLED_GATE_.mirror_side_not_yet_tested: USDMXN/riskshockcontinuation_long (fading US500 down-shocks) was diagnosed as weaker than the short side at every quantile during Phase 1 and was not built this cycle -- lower priority given the short side's own cost-drag failure.

STCMOMENTUMTURN_LONG_KILLED_DEGENERATE_T.self_test: FAILED: only 1 model row (degenerate, not simple rarity). Root cause: STC's distribution is heavily zero-inflated and floor-bounded at 0 (median~0.0001, 75th pct~10.9 on USDMXN) -- asking for a LOW rolling-rank against a feature already pinned at its floor most of the time is nearly unsatisfiable, since ties at the floor push the rank UP (fraction of window <= current), not down. This is a threshold-direction mismatch on a zero-inflated feature, not an economic-rarity finding.

final_disposition_2026-10-09_phase2_batc.summary: 14 new single-asset USDMXN theses (7 mechanisms x 2 sides: MACD histogram acceleration, Stochastic K-D spread, Williams %R, ROC momentum, Donchian distance, NATR regime, Bollinger %B), built applying lessons from the recalibration round (looser default quantile 0.90/0.10, single-condition only, no AND-conditions). 0/14 passed Gate A. All 14 cleared the row floor comfortably on the first try (no recalibration needed this time -- validates that the 0.90/0.10 default was the right fix). Two near-misses flagged: macdhistaccel_long/short showed decent gross signal but typical ~0.04-0.05 cost gap; rocmomentum_short was the standout at net_mean_R=-0.0157 (gross=0.0488), the second-closest default-grid result in the whole USDMXN search after stcmomentumturn_short. natrregime_long/short were found to share an identical un-differentiated event population (a spec design gap, not a bug) -- noted for any future generator revision.

final_disposition_2026-10-07_single_asse.summary: 20 genuinely new single-asset USDMXN theses (10 mechanisms x 2 sides, built via a parameterized generator after the cross-asset approach was abandoned per user instruction). 0/20 passed. Only 4/20 (exhaustionreversal_short/long, liquiditysweepreversal_short/long) even cleared the 2000-row floor to reach Gate A, and all 4 died cleanly there (0 positive net_mean_R). The other 16 died at the row floor before any gate -- notably worse floor-survival than the earlier 16-mechanism ported batch (which had 12/16 reach Gate A). Methodology lesson for future batches: the single-feature rolling-rank-at-5%-quantile-over-500-bars template structurally lands just under USDMXN's 2000-row floor for MOST generic TA/statistical features at this bar density -- next time, default to a looser quantile (e.g. 0.90) or shorter rolling-rank lookback rather than 0.95/500 bars, and avoid stacking a second AND condition (every dual-condition mechanism in this batch -- rsidivergencereversal, waveletcleantrend, bbsqueezebreakout -- died at the floor, several by a wide margin). Also found and fixed one real methodology bug (not a mechanical mistake unique to one edge): STC's zero-inflated/floor-bounded distribution makes a LOW-rolling-rank trigger nearly unsatisfiable regardless of economic merit -- a lesson for choosing which features suit a quantile-rank trigger at all. Also confirmed and fixed a resource-contention bug: running multiple self-tests for the same asset in parallel races on a shared live-HMM-regime-continuation cache file (WinError 5 Access Denied) -- self-tests/exports for the same asset must run serially; only the persisted-artifact-based Gate A sweep is safe to run concurrently with them.
